title: feat(eip155): add Shibarium (eip155:109) as a known network
body:
Registers Shibarium (eip155:109) as a known network with its bridged USDC (`0xf010f12dcA0b96D2d6685bf4dB3dbB4Ad500B6Ad`, 6 decimals).

This USDC implements neither EIP-3009 nor EIP-2612, so it is configured as `AssetTransferMethod::Permit2`. Permit2 (`0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3`) and both x402 Permit2 proxies — exact (`0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001`) and upto (`0x4020A4f3b7b90ccA423B9fabCc0CE57C6C240002`) — are deployed on Shibarium at their canonical addresses, so both schemes work.

Changes follow the existing Celo pattern: network name table in `x402-types`, `KnownNetworkEip155` for `ChainId` and `USDC`, a unit test, and a README line. `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` pass for both crates.

Question for maintainers: the `Permit2` variant requires `name` and `version`. `name` is the token's on-chain `name()`, but the token exposes no `version()`; I've used `"1"`, and the Permit2 signing path doesn't read it. Happy to change it.

title: feat(eip155): reconcile a retried settle with the transaction already broadcast
body:
Stacked on #138, the #136 fix: this branch has the #138 commit and one more, so review #138 first; the second commit is this change. It is the follow-up #138 mentions under "Not in this PR". With #138, `/settle` answers `settlement_pending` (HTTP 202) with the transaction hash when the receipt cannot be fetched after the broadcast. A resource server on the reference SDK then retries `/settle` once with the same payload (`settleWithPendingRetry` in `@x402/core` 2.28.0), and the reference facilitator answers that retry from a `PendingSettlementStore`. x402-rs has no such store, so it verifies the retry from scratch. Once the first transaction has landed, that fails with `FiatTokenV2: authorization is used or canceled` (500, `unexpected_error`, empty `transaction`), and the resource server answers its client 402: the buyer has paid, gets no data, and the hash from the 202 is gone. ### What changes - New `chain/pending_settlement.rs`: a `PendingSettlementStore` trait and `InMemoryPendingSettlementStore` (a `DashMap`, entries kept 5 minutes like `PENDING_SETTLEMENT_TTL_MS` in the reference). Entries are keyed by the hash of the payment's signature and hold the transaction hash and a hash of the settle request (payload and requirements). - `Eip155MetaTransactionProvider` gains `pending_settlements` and `find_receipt`, with defaults (no store, no lookup) so other implementors keep the current behaviour. `Eip155ChainProvider` keeps one in-memory store and looks the receipt up every second for up to `receipt_timeout_secs`. - `settle_with_pending_store` wraps the settle paths #138 changed: v1 exact, v2 exact (EIP-3009, and Permit2 with and without EIP-2612) and v2 upto. When a settlement ends with the receipt unavailable, it records the hash. A later request with the same signature and the same request hash is not verified or sent again: it takes the entry and answers success once the receipt is found, a failure if the transaction reverted, or `settlement_pending` with the same hash (and puts the entry back) if the receipt is still unavailable. Any other request settles as before. - Two choices beyond the reference: the request hash must match, so a signature re-sent with other requirements settles from scratch (and fails on the used authorization) instead of inheriting another request's settlement; and the entry is taken before reconciling, so two copies of the same retry cannot both answer success. - The success answer's `payer` now comes from the payload's authorization, the same address the verified payment was built from, because a reconciled retry skips verification. ### Tests 16 new unit tests: the store (take once, another request leaves the entry, TTL, remove, request hash, key), the receipt polling (lookups recover, timeout), and the settle wrapper on a mock provider (a receipt failure is recorded; a retry reconciles without sending again; a retry while the receipt is still unavailable stays pending with the same hash and reconciles later; reverted is a failure; the same signature in another request settles from scratch; success and failures before the broadcast record nothing; no store settles from scratch; `Arc

` forwards). Checks in `rust:trixie` (cargo 1.99.0), the image the Dockerfile builds in: `cargo fmt --all --check` passes; the Dockerfile's build command (`cargo build --package x402-facilitator --features full --release --locked`) passes; `cargo test -p x402-chain-eip155 --features full` 37 pass (34 unit, 3 doc); `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` 129 pass and 1 fail, the same `x402-chain-tron` `networks::tests::permit2_proxies` failure as on main; both clippy runs report the same warnings as main; `cargo check` of the facilitator (with `x402-chain-eip155/full`), `x402-types` and `x402-facilitator-local` with Rust 1.93.0, the workspace `rust-version`, passes. ### Reproduction on Base Sepolia The facilitator (#138, then this branch, default `receipt_timeout_secs` of 30) signs with a testnet key, and its only RPC is a proxy to sepolia.base.org that answers HTTP 503 (`-32011 no backend is currently healthy to serve traffic`) to every receipt lookup of the settlement for a window after the broadcast. Resource server on `@x402/express` 2.28.0, client on `@x402/fetch` 2.28.0, one paid call ($0.01 in test USDC) per row, two where the app calls again. "The app calls again" is a second paid call after the 402, as an application might make. I read every settlement below back from two public endpoints: status 1, sent by the signer, one 0.01 USDC transfer from the buyer to the seller, and `AuthorizationUsed` for the nonce the client signed. title: fix(eip155): keep the hash and answer settlement_pending when the receipt fetch fails
body:
Closes #136.

When the RPC failed while the facilitator waited for the receipt of a transaction it had already broadcast, `/settle` answered 500 with `transaction: ""` and `errorReason: "unexpected_error"`, the same answer as a failure before anything was sent. The transfer could still land, and the caller had no hash to check it with.

### What changes

- `Eip155ChainProvider::send_transaction` keeps the hash once the submission returns one. If the receipt watcher then fails (an RPC error, a null receipt or the timeout), it looks the receipt up three more times, waiting 1, 2 and 4 seconds before each lookup, with the same confirmation count. A receipt found that way settles as before, revert check included.
- If the receipt is still unknown, it resets the nonce as before and returns the new `MetaTransactionSendError::ReceiptUnavailable { tx_hash, source }`.
- The settlement paths (v1 exact, v2 exact with EIP-3009 and Permit2, v2 upto) turn that error into the new `X402SchemeFacilitatorError::SettlementPending { network, transaction, details }`. `ErrorReason` gains `SettlementPending`, serialized as `settlement_pending`.
- `/settle` answers it with 202, `success: false`, `errorReason: "settlement_pending"`, the hash in `transaction` and the request's network in `network`. An error before the submission returned a hash still answers 500 with an empty `transaction`, so the two cases stay distinguishable (ask 2 in the issue).

### Tests

12 unit tests, next to the code they cover:

- `x402-types`: `SettlementPending` serializes as `settlement_pending` and maps to that payment problem; `OnchainFailure` still maps to `unexpected_error`.
- `x402-chain-eip155`: the lookup retry finds a receipt after failed lookups, stops at the first receipt, and gives up after three lookups with 1, 2 and 4 s waits (paused tokio clock). A receipt error or a receipt timeout after broadcast becomes `SettlementPending` with the hash and the network; a transport error before broadcast and a reverted transaction stay failures.
- `x402-facilitator-local`: the pending answer carries `transaction` and `network` with status 202; an on-chain failure still has an empty `transaction` and status 500.

I ran these on this branch and on main e75adda8 in `rust:trixie` (cargo 1.99.0), the image the Dockerfile builds in: `cargo fmt --all --check`; the Dockerfile's `cargo build --package x402-facilitator --features full --release --locked`; `cargo test` for the three crates (`x402-chain-eip155` with `--features full`) and for the workspace; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo clippy -p x402-chain-eip155 --features full --all-targets`; and `cargo check` of the facilitator (with `x402-chain-eip155/full`), `x402-types` and `x402-facilitator-local` with Rust 1.93.0, the workspace `rust-version`. All pass, except that `cargo test --workspace` has one failure, `x402-chain-tron` `networks::tests::permit2_proxies`, which fails the same way on main. Clippy reports the same warnings as on main, none in the changed code.

### Reproduction

I reproduced the issue on a local fork of Celo mainnet: anvil forking forno.celo.org (chain id 42220, 1 s blocks) with Circle's USDC (0xcebA9300f2b948710d2653dD7B07f33A8B32118C), and the facilitator pointed only at a small JSON-RPC proxy in front of anvil. Once armed, the proxy forwards the next `eth_sendRawTransaction`, so the transfer is broadcast and mined, and then fails the receipt lookups for that transaction for a set window: HTTP 503 with the `-32011 no backend is currently healthy to serve traffic` body from the issue, a `null` result, or a 503 to every call other than `eth_sendRawTransaction`. Each `/settle` answer is checked against the chain, read from anvil directly: `authorizationState(payer, nonce)`, the `AuthorizationUsed` log and the transaction that emitted it.

| Fault (settles) | main e75adda8 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| none (2) | 2 success | 2 success |
| receipt lookups answer 503 for 2.5 s after broadcast (5) | 5 failed, all 5 landed | 5 success with the hash |
| receipt lookups answer 503 for 60 s (5) | 5 failed, all 5 landed | 5 pending with the hash |
| receipt lookups answer `null` for 60 s (3) | 3 failed, all 3 landed | 3 pending with the hash |
| every RPC call other than `eth_sendRawTransaction` answers 503 for 30 s after broadcast (3) | 3 failed, all 3 landed | 3 pending with the hash |
| receipt lookups answer 503 for 60 s, x402 v2 payload (3) | 3 failed, all 3 landed | 3 pending with the hash |
| `eth_sendRawTransaction` answers 503, nothing broadcast (3) | 3 failed, none landed | 3 failed, none landed |

"Failed" is 500 with `success: false`, `unexpected_error` and an empty `transaction`. "Pending" is 202 with `settlement_pending`, `network` set, and in `transaction` the hash of the transaction that used the authorization. Each authorization was used at most once. The 2.0.1 image from the issue gave the same answers as main.

Harness and logs: https://github.com/zachsplat/x402-rs-136-repro

### Notes for review

- Latency: only the failure path changes. The three lookups add about 7 s after the watcher fails, so a watcher that times out now answers after `receipt_timeout_secs` plus about 7 s. The attempts and the first wait are constants in `provider.rs`; I can make them configurable.
- Status 202, because the payment may still complete. The TypeScript `HTTPFacilitatorClient` reads a 2xx answer as a `SettleResponse` instead of throwing, and the Go client turns a non-200 answer that has an `errorReason` into a `SettleError` that keeps `transaction` and `network`, so both see `settlement_pending` with the hash. Another status is a one-line change in `handlers.rs`.
- v1: the reference SDKs return `settlement_pending` for v2 only. I return it for v1 exact as well, because the case in #136 is a v1 payment and x402-rs uses one `ErrorReason` for both versions. I can limit it to v2.
- Not in this PR: reconciling a retry. The reference resource servers retry `/settle` once with the same payload after `settlement_pending`, and the reference facilitators answer that retry from a `PendingSettlementStore` (x402 docs, core-concepts/facilitator, "Settlement pending and auto-recovery"). x402-rs has no such store, so the retry is verified from scratch, and once the first transfer has landed it fails with `FiatTokenV2: authorization is used or canceled` (500, empty `transaction`). The reproduction shows this with a second `/settle` of the same payload; nothing is charged twice. I can add an in-memory store in a follow-up.
- Related: #119. This sets `network` only on the pending answer.

title: eip155 settle: an RPC error while waiting for the receipt is reported as OnchainFailure with an empty transaction, although the transfer was broadcast and mined
body:
**What happens**

When the RPC fails while the facilitator is waiting for the receipt of a transaction it has **already broadcast**, `/settle` answers `500` with `success: false`, `transaction: ""` and `errorReason: "unexpected_error"`. The transfer is on chain, and the response gives the caller no way to know that.

Observed on `ghcr.io/x402-rs/x402-facilitator@sha256:8eb27a73…` (2.0.1, rev `de2e55bc`), Celo mainnet (eip155:42220): one signer, one HTTP RPC, settlements serialised to one in flight. The code path below is unchanged on `main` (`e75adda8`).

Example (EIP-3009 USDC, x402 v1):

```
11:08:26.7  POST /settle received
11:08:28    transferWithAuthorization mined, block 79470550, status 1,
            tx 0xa5f6a7027df46b5da388406fbc39e468f2466968f698ffbd21ad0e674af58601
11:08:44.6  WARN Settlement failed error=Settlement(OnchainFailure("HTTP error 503 with body:
            {\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"error\":{\"code\":-32011,\"message\":\"no backend is currently healthy to serve traffic\"},\"id\":460671}\n"))
            status=500 elapsed=17868ms
```

Response body: `{"success":false,"network":"celo","transaction":"","errorReason":"unexpected_error","errorMessage":"HTTP error 503 with body: {…-32011…}","payer":"0x…"}`.

**How often:** over about 2.8 days and about 11,700 settles, 19 settles failed with this RPC 503. For 17 of them (EIP-3009) we checked `authorizationState(payer, nonce)` and found the `AuthorizationUsed` log:
- **9 were consumed by that same request**, mined 1–10 s after it started.
- 8 were never consumed.

The response cannot tell the two apart: same status, same `errorReason`, same `errorMessage`, empty `transaction`. Facilitator latency doesn't separate them either (the ranges overlap at about 10.5 s).

**Where**

- `crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/chain/provider.rs` (`main` `e75adda8`): `send_transaction` gets a `PendingTransactionBuilder` back at L300, then calls `watcher.get_receipt()` at L317. On error it returns `MetaTransactionSendError::PendingTransaction(e)` (L322). The transaction hash, which `pending_tx` already holds, is dropped.
- `crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/v1_eip155_exact/facilitator.rs` L1058–1059 maps both `Eip155ExactError::Transport(_)` (an error **before** the send: `estimate_gas`, `send_transaction`) and `Eip155ExactError::PendingTransaction(_)` (an error **after** it) to the same `OnchainFailure(value.to_string())`. `handlers.rs` L303 then answers 500 for both.

Our reading: the 8 unconsumed cases are the 503 hitting a pre-send call, and the 9 consumed ones are the 503 hitting the receipt poll. We could not confirm this from the logs, because both produce the identical message.

**Impact**

A resource server that trusts the answer withholds the resource from a buyer who paid. A client that retries with a fresh authorization charges the payer a second time. Any metering layer in front of the facilitator refunds a settlement that happened.

**Ask**

1. Keep the hash once the send has succeeded. Read `*pending_tx.tx_hash()` before `get_receipt()`, and on a receipt error return it, for example as a variant that carries the hash. Then either:
   - retry the receipt read (`get_transaction_receipt(hash)`) a few times before giving up, or
   - answer with `transaction: <hash>` and `errorReason: "settlement_pending"`, which the spec allows exactly when `transaction` is non-empty.
2. Keep pre-send and post-send failures distinguishable in the response. A transport error before `send_transaction` returned means nothing was broadcast and the caller can safely retry. An error after it does not mean that.

Related: #119 (empty `network` on failure responses, the same response shape) and #117 (failure bodies embed the transport error text).

Timestamps, payload nonces and tx hashes for all 19 are available on request.

title: x402-axum does not apply payment-response Cache-Control policy
body:
## Missing payment-response cache policy in x402-axum

`x402-axum` 2.0.2 does not automatically apply a cache policy to payment challenges or responses carrying payment receipts. The same behavior is present at current commit `e75adda8a0e3cf23db446883ba91b88bbab2fe28`.

- Verification failures construct HTTP 402 or 412 with `Payment-Required`, but no `Cache-Control`.
- Settlement failures construct HTTP 402 without `Cache-Control`.
- Successful settlement adds `Payment-Response` to the handler response without making it private. A handler's `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` therefore remains unchanged.

Source: [challenge and failure response construction](https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/e75adda8a0e3cf23db446883ba91b88bbab2fe28/crates/x402-axum/src/paygate.rs#L325-L374), [settlement before handler execution](https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/e75adda8a0e3cf23db446883ba91b88bbab2fe28/crates/x402-axum/src/paygate.rs#L537-L560), and [settlement after handler execution](https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/e75adda8a0e3cf23db446883ba91b88bbab2fe28/crates/x402-axum/src/paygate.rs#L562-L591).

## How to observe

1. Protect an Axum route with the middleware and request it without payment. Inspect the 402 response: it has no automatic `Cache-Control: no-store`.
2. Have the handler return `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` and complete a successful verification/settlement (a test facilitator suffices). The response carries `Payment-Response`, but the handler's public cache policy remains unchanged.

Whether a response is actually cached depends on the deployment's proxy/cache configuration. The missing functionality is an automatic payment-aware cache policy, not a claim that every deployment caches these responses.

## Parity with the Foundation SDKs

The Foundation SDKs provide a policy of `no-store` for payment challenges and allowance responses, and `private` for completed payment receipt responses while preserving other handler directives. See [TypeScript constants/helper](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/7f2b2f1f77fa5317615735e3378a6fad41cccb4e/typescript/packages/core/src/http/x402HTTPResourceServer.ts#L30-L50) and the earlier Foundation issue https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/2955.

Please consider equivalent handling in the Axum middleware, without altering unrelated routes. When recognizing an existing `private` directive, commas inside quoted extension values must not be treated as separators.

title: feat(eip155): append an ERC-8021 attribution tag to EIP-3009 settlement calldata
body:
## Summary

Facilitator side of the [x402 extension keyed `builder-code`](docs/specs/extensions/builder_code.md) for the `v2-eip155-exact` scheme. ERC-8021 calls this transaction attribution, so the code and config use "attribution tag"; `builder-code` is kept as the wire key only. At settlement the facilitator appends an ERC-8021 Schema 2 suffix to the calldata:

- `w` is the facilitator's own code, from the scheme config key `attribution_tag`
- `a` and `s` are read from the payment's `builder-code` extension

The EVM ignores trailing calldata, so `transferWithAuthorization` executes unchanged.

## What changed since the first draft

~~Extension key `attribution`, own spec document `docs/specs/extensions/attribution.md`, config key `attributionWalletCode`.~~ Reworked to follow the spec already in this repo:

- extension key is `builder-code`; the separate spec document is gone
- codes are read from `info` (what the reference clients send) and unwrapped (what the spec examples show)
- `s` is accepted as a string or an array, capped at 10 entries like the reference implementation
- config key is `attribution_tag`, snake_case like `eip2612_gas_sponsoring`
- with a tag configured, `/supported` lists `builder-code` under `extensions`
- rebased onto `main`, conflicts with the telemetry change resolved

Naming: the module, config key and docs say "attribution tag" (the ERC-8021 term); the wire key stays `builder-code` because that is what clients and resource servers send.

## Backwards compatibility

No `attribution_tag` and no codes in the payment: the calldata is byte-identical to `main`.

## Judgement calls, all reversible

1. **A request code that fails `^[a-z0-9_]{1,32}$` is left out and the payment still settles.** The spec says invalid codes must be rejected. The reference facilitator drops them, and a bad tag should not block a payment. One-line change if you want it strict.
2. **The facilitator does not compare the payment's `a` with the declared one.** The settle request carries the payment's extensions only, not the `402` response, so the facilitator has nothing to compare against. The reference facilitator does not check it either, and the current upstream spec no longer lists that step for the facilitator; the copy vendored here dates from 2026-06-16.
3. **A malformed `attribution_tag` makes `build` fail**, so the scheme handler is not registered. A facilitator asked to tag must not silently run untagged.
4. **`/supported` advertises `builder-code` only when a tag is configured**, so the response is unchanged for a facilitator that did not opt in. Payments that carry codes are tagged either way.
5. **Names `attribution_tag` (config) and `attribution_tag.rs` (module).** Happy to rename.

## What this does not do

- Permit2, EIP-2612, `upto` and V1 settlements stay untagged. Follow-up: #130
- No resource-server or client helpers for declaring codes.
- A config value of the wrong JSON type still falls back to the default config, as before. Only a string that fails the pattern is an error.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is not touched; its latest entry is 2.0.0.

## Verification

Head `097bc7c`. The unit suite (31 passed) was re-run on that commit. The mutation run, the fork run and the live settlement were run on `485dc9d`; the only difference between the two is doc comments and one test name, no code path changed.

title: Axum V2 settlement failures omit the Payment-Response receipt header
body:
## Behavior

With `x402-axum` 2.0.2 and its default verify → handler → settle ordering, a facilitator returning `success: false` correctly prevents delivery of the handler's successful response. However, the resulting HTTP 402 response has no `Payment-Response` header. It contains only a JSON error with a textual description of the settlement failure.

This differs from the Node `@x402/core` 2.27.0 HTTP resource server, which returns the structured failed settlement result in `Payment-Response` along with HTTP 402. A client can then read the error reason and any transaction/network fields using the same receipt decoder as for successful settlement.

## Reproduction

Use a facilitator implementation that returns successful verification, then returns this settlement result:

```json
{"success":false,"errorReason":"declined","transaction":"tx","network":"inflow:1"}
```

Attach a V2 static price tag to an Axum route whose handler returns HTTP 200. Send a matching V2 `Payment-Signature` so verification and settlement are reached. The response is HTTP 402, but `response.headers().get("Payment-Response")` is `None`.

I reproduced this with a real Axum Router and the published middleware; only the facilitator response was controlled. No live payment is needed.

## Source

In [`paygate.rs` at v2.0.2](https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/v2.0.2/crates/x402-axum/src/paygate.rs), `validate_settlement` converts a failed structured receipt into `PaygateError::Settlement(String)` (lines 654–674). The V2 settlement-error response builder returns the JSON error without a receipt header (lines 359–373).

Could the failed settlement receipt be retained and encoded into `Payment-Response`, while preserving the existing refusal to deliver the successful resource? Transport failures without a settlement receipt are a separate case; this report concerns a valid structured `success: false` result.

title: Exact Permit2 client lacks EIP-2612 sponsorship enrichment available in Node and Rust upto
body:
## Exact Permit2 Buyer sponsorship parity

In `x402-chain-eip155` 2.0.2, `V2Eip155ExactClient` signs the Permit2 payment but copies an advertised `eip2612GasSponsoring` declaration into the payload without generating the signed EIP-2612 allowance permit.

The Node `@x402/evm` 2.27.0 exact client calls `trySignEip2612PermitExtension`: when the extension is advertised, the necessary signer/RPC capabilities are available, and allowance is insufficient, it creates the permit. Rust's `upto` client already has separate `try_eip2612_gas_sponsoring` support, but the exact client does not.

### Reproduction

1. Construct a V2 `exact` offer with `extra.assetTransferMethod = "permit2"` and an `eip2612GasSponsoring` declaration.
2. Pass it to `V2Eip155ExactClient::accept` and sign the resulting candidate using a local `PrivateKeySigner`.
3. Decode the payment header. The payment contains a signed `permit2Authorization`, but the sponsorship extension remains the unchanged server declaration, with no allowance-permit signature.

I reproduced this through the actual 2.0.2 candidate signer using a disposable local key; no blockchain transaction was submitted.

### Relevant source

- Rust: `x402-chain-eip155/src/v2_eip155_exact/client.rs`, `PayloadSigner::sign_payment` copies `self.extensions` in both branches.
- Rust: `x402-chain-eip155/src/v2_eip155_upto/client.rs`, `try_eip2612_gas_sponsoring` implements the separate upto path.
- Node: `typescript/packages/mechanisms/evm/src/exact/client/scheme.ts`, `createPaymentPayload` invokes the EIP-2612 helper for Permit2.

Could the exact client provide equivalent optional allowance-permit generation? Ordinary Permit2 payments with existing allowance remain a separate, working use case. This request is specifically for exact-scheme sponsorship parity, not a new payment protocol.

title: x402-reqwest signs before rejecting a non-replayable request body
body:
## Problem

In `x402-reqwest 2.0.2`, automatic payment handling invokes the payment signer before rejecting a request whose streaming body cannot be replayed.

The request can therefore fail with `RequestNotCloneable` after signing has already occurred. A signer may involve an interactive approval or another externally visible operation, so the replay check should precede it.

## Source

[`X402Client::handle`](https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/0b14f39afb604a7df25b3496ba34122bdca45a7f/crates/x402-reqwest/src/client.rs) performs these operations in order:

1. Saves `req.try_clone()` as an `Option`.
2. Sends the original request.
3. On HTTP 402, calls `make_payment_headers`, which selects and signs a payment.
4. Checks the saved clone and returns `RequestNotCloneable` when it is absent.

## Reproduction

I reproduced this against the published crate on Rust 1.93.0:

- Construct a POST body using `reqwest::Body::wrap_stream`.
- Register a scheme whose `PaymentCandidateSigner::sign_payment` increments an atomic counter and returns a valid header string.
- Put a terminal test transport after the real `X402Client` middleware, returning a parseable HTTP 402 response.
- Send the request through the middleware.

Actual result: `RequestNotCloneable`, with the signer counter equal to **1**. The test uses the real upstream selection/signing/retry path; only the HTTP response and signer are test doubles. No live payment is made.

## Expected behavior

On the HTTP 402 path, reject an unavailable retry request before invoking payment selection/signing. Ordinary non-402 responses can still be returned without requiring a replayable body. This does not require buffering arbitrary streams.

title: Add a Nano (XNO) chain crate: a feeless  settlement rail with a block as the receipt
body:
x402-rs already models settlement as pluggable chain adaptors (EIP-155 for EVM, solana, aptos), each implementing the facilitator/payment trait. A Nano (XNO) chain would fit that exact seam — no new protocol concept, just another chain backend.

Why it maps cleanly:
- Nano's native `exact` payment scheme is a single signed send block; the amount is fixed in the block like a USDC exact-payment, so it drops into the existing exact-scheme verification path.
- Feeless and final in ~seconds, so a facilitator's settle step costs nothing and has no gas-oracle or nonce bookkeeping.
- The block hash is itself the public, append-only receipt — a facilitator could return the tx hash as the settlement proof with no extra indexing.
- An agent that only holds XNO (no EVM/Solana/Aptos wallet, no gas) could still pay a protected route.

Concretely I'd expect a crate like `x402-chain-nano` mirroring the existing chain crates: a facilitator that builds the send block from the challenge's `payTo`/`amount`, submits via the public Nano RPC (poein.work or app.nano.to for mainnet), and exposes a `verify` that a block with the right amount to the right account exists on-ledger.

For the verification leg there is a callable reference you can test against today (live, settled in XNO, no signup): https://extract.paypercall.dev/api/v1/nano-info returns balance, representative, block count, frontier and pending for any Nano address; https://extract.paypercall.dev/api/v1/address-verdict labels whether a payTo address is a real active counterparty. Both accept GET ?account=nano_...

title: Proposal: add Nano (XNO) as a settlement chain alongside EVM/Solana/Aptos
body:
## Proposal: Nano (XNO) settlement support

The x402-rs facilitator already supports EVM (EIP-155), Solana and Aptos chains through the modular chain provider pattern. This proposal suggests adding Nano (XNO) as a settlement chain — a feeless, single-block-final, green rail that shares none of the gas-cost overhead of EVM or Solana.

### Why Nano fits the architecture

The `ChainProvider` enum and `x402-chain-*` crate pattern in x402-rs is designed for additive chain support. Adding Nano would follow the same boundaries as the existing providers:

- **x402-chain-nano** — a new crate implementing Nano send-block verification (state-block hash + frontier check), preimage parsing (raw 30-decimal units match x402 exact-scheme amounts), and RPC via the Nano protocol (rpc.nano.to or a self-hosted Nano node).
- **Scheme**: the `exact` scheme already proven for Nano in the x402 specification (x402-foundation/x402 exact-nano-mainnet spec). An exact-amount Nano payment is a send block to a per-checkout receive address, which the facilitator verifies by inspecting the Nano ledger.
- **No gas overhead**: Nano payments settle in ~0.2-1.5 seconds with zero network fee. The facilitator covers no gas — Nano has no gas — so there is no sponsored-gas wallet to maintain.

### What already exists

Nano x402 tooling is live and MIT-licensed:
- `@x402nano/exact` (npm) — exact-scheme payload construction/parsing for Nano
- `x402nano/facilitator` (GitHub) — reference Nano facilitator implementing verify/settle
- `pursekeeper/x402-nano-exact` (PyPI) — Python implementation of the exact Nano x402 scheme

These would serve as reference implementations for an x402-rs native Nano provider, no reverse-engineering needed.

### The ask

Would x402-rs accept a `x402-chain-nano` crate that adds Nano as a settlement chain, following the existing `x402-chain-eip155-provider` boundaries? I can open a draft PR with:
- Nano RPC client (`NanoRPC` struct wrapping the Nano protocol JSON-RPC)
- Send-block verification (destination-address match, frontier confirmation, raw amount parsing)
- Integration into the `ChainProvider` enum
- Unit tests + one live test against the Nano test network

Nano is instant (sub-second finality), feeless (zero gas), and green (BTC-equivalent 0.000112 kWh/tx). For x402 sub-cent agent payments, the per-call cost is *exactly* the price of the endpoint — no settlement fee floor. This is the cheapest settlement rail available for agent-machine payments.

NANO ONLY under the repository rules: this proposal exists because Nano is the cheapest feeless rail for sub-cent x402 settlement. If x402-rs should not carry a Nano chain, close this and I will not re-open it.

title: Add crates/x402-chain-nano beside eip155/solana/aptos/tron — the settle step has no relayer work
body:
# Add crates/chains/x402-chain-nano beside eip155/solana/aptos/tron — the settle step has no relayer work

## Proposal, in the project's own terms

`x402-rs` is a workspace of one crate per chain (`x402-chain-eip155`, `x402-chain-solana`, `x402-chain-aptos`, `x402-chain-tron`), each with a facilitator because on every existing rail a buyer cannot move value without gas. This proposes one more chain crate: **`x402-chain-nano`**, on the ground that its settlement step has no relayer work at all.

The structural point, matching the repo's existing layout (`src/networks.rs`, the per-chain facilitator crates):

- Every crate the repo has needs a facilitator because a buyer cannot move value without gas. On Nano (XNO) that premise disappears: the buyer publishes its own signed send block (Nano RPC `process`) and there is no gas for a relayer to sponsor.
- The settlement leg reduces to a single verify: the block exists, is a `send` subtype to `payTo` (read from the block, not the request body), `received == sent` (fee is structurally zero — no separate fee computation), and the block is cemented-or-unknown (final by publication). **`/settle` has nothing to await from a chain.**

## What changes (additive)

A `x402-chain-nano` crate mirroring the existing chain crates:

1. `verify`: Nano `block_info` once — `{confirmed: "true", subtype: "send", link_as_account == payTo}`; assert `received == sent`.
2. `settle`: single `block_info` read for cementation; success with `fee = 0`. No `feePayer`, no relayer, no nonce, no signer, no re-broadcast.
3. Match the workspace's crate layout (`src/networks.rs` entry + `v2_nano_exact/facilitator.rs`), and the feature/config wiring the existing crates use.

The `src/networks.rs` registry gains a `nano:mainnet` entry; nothing existing is touched.

## Runnable reference

The mechanism is proven on a live x402 seller preview: settlement reduces to a single dependency-free verify (Nano RPC — `process`, `block_info`, `representative`, docs.nano.org), receive-only `payTo`, `fee = 0` from the block. A 9/9-tested verification leg is available on request.

Happy to open the corresponding `crates/x402-chain-nano` PR once the chain crate is accepted.

fix(types): redact URLs in on-chain failure details before they reach a response body
body:
## Summary

Closes #117. A transport error's Display embeds the request URL (measured with alloy 1.x: `error sending request for url (http://host/v2/<key>)`), and `OnchainFailure(e.to_string())` carries that text into `PaymentProblem` details → `error_message` (settle) / `invalid_reason_details` (verify). For hosted RPC providers that is the API key in an HTTP response body.

## Change

`x402_types::scheme::redact_urls(&str) -> String`, applied in `as_payment_problem` for `OnchainFailure` — the one chokepoint every chain crate (eip155, tron, aptos) funnels through. Each `scheme://…` in the text becomes `scheme://host[:port]/<redacted>`: path, query, fragment and userinfo are cut; a bare host or a lone trailing slash is left as is, so the caller still learns which endpoint failed. No dependency added (no `url` crate in `x402-types`); hand-rolled scan with tests.

Tests: key as path segment / query string / userinfo (each asserts the secret is absent from the output), bare hosts and URL-free text unchanged, two URLs in one message.

## What this does not do

- Does not touch server-side logs (#115 covers the startup line; a `tracing::error!` of the raw transport error elsewhere would still carry the URL — I did not find one in the eip155 crate).
- Does not change `ErrorReason` or status codes.

## Verification

```
cargo fmt -p x402-types -- --check          clean
cargo clippy -p x402-types --all-targets    no new warnings
```

title: fix(eip155): resend once when the node rejects a submission with 'fee cap less than base fee'
body:
## Summary

Refs #113 (ask 2 of the issue; ask 1, headroom over the estimated base fee, is not changed here). When the node rejects a submission with `fee cap less than base fee` — the fee filler priced against the block it saw and the next block's base fee moved above the cap — nothing was broadcast and the nonce was not consumed, but the error surfaced as `unexpected_error`. Observed on Celo mainnet: 2 of 1,005 settlements in a Permit2 soak, both transient, both fine on a resend seconds later.

## Change

`Eip155ChainProvider::send_transaction` resends **exactly once** for that rejection, after the existing nonce reset, with fees refilled against the newer block (the request carries no fees itself; the filler prices it on each `send_transaction`). A `tracing::warn!` records the retry under the `telemetry` feature. Every other submission error is surfaced exactly as before.

`is_fee_cap_below_base_fee(&str) -> bool` is a `pub fn` matching the geth phrasing (`fee cap less than base fee`) and op-geth's (`max fee per gas less than block base fee`), case-insensitively, anywhere in the transport error's message. Tests: both phrasings inside the full `-32000` transport message; `nonce too low`, `insufficient funds`, `replacement transaction underpriced` and a connection reset are not retried.

## What this does not do

- No headroom on `maxFeePerGas` (ask 1) — that is a fee-policy decision for the maintainers (`2 × baseFee + tip` is what most wallets do). Happy to follow up if wanted; this PR stands without it.
- The legacy (non-EIP-1559) path re-sends with the gas price it already fetched; the rejection is an EIP-1559 message, so the retry is not expected to trigger there.
- No `Retry-After` classification at the facilitator API layer.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p x402-chain-eip155 --features full fee_cap_tests    3 passed
cargo fmt -p x402-chain-eip155 -- --check                         clean
cargo clippy -p x402-chain-eip155 --features full --all-targets   no new warnings
```

title: verify/settle error bodies embed the transport error text, which carries the keyed RPC URL
body:
## Summary

A transport error's text reaches the facilitator's HTTP response body, and with alloy 1.x that text embeds the request URL — for hosted RPC providers, the API key.

## Measured

alloy `ProviderBuilder::new().connect_http("http://127.0.0.1:9/v2/SECRETKEY123")`, then any call:

```
display: error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:9/v2/SECRETKEY123)
contains_secret: true
```

## Path

- `crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/v1_eip155_exact/facilitator.rs:1058` — `Eip155ExactError::Transport(_) => Self::OnchainFailure(value.to_string())`
- `crates/x402-types/src/scheme/mod.rs:144` — `OnchainFailure(e) => PaymentProblem::new(ErrorReason::UnexpectedError, e.to_string())`
- `crates/x402-facilitator-local/src/handlers.rs:238-280` — `problem.details()` becomes `invalid_reason_details` (verify) and `error_message` (settle) in the JSON response.

So any transport failure during verify or settle — RPC down, timeout, 429, DNS — answers the caller with the keyed RPC URL in the body. Callers are resource servers and, through them, sometimes end clients; response bodies are logged and pasted far more freely than container logs.

## Related

#114 / #115 cover the startup log line. This is the other place the issue asked about ("any other place a provider URL is logged or included in an error message"); it is a different fix-unit (error construction, not logging), hence its own issue.

## Suggested fix

Redact URLs when the transport error is turned into an `OnchainFailure` / `PaymentProblem`: replace `scheme://host/anything` with `scheme://host/<redacted>` (the helper from #115 fits, applied over the message with a URL regex), or drop the transport text from the client-facing `details` altogether and keep it in a server-side `tracing::error!` — redacted there too. A unit test asserting the response `details` never contains a path/query/userinfo from the configured URL.

title: Redact credentials from rpc_url in the provider startup log (userinfo, query string, key path segments)
body:
## Summary

On startup the facilitator logs the full RPC URL:

```
INFO x402_chain_eip155::chain::provider: Using HTTP transport chain=eip155:… rpc_url=https://… rate_limit=…
```

`crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/chain/provider.rs:100-102`:

```rust
let rpc_url = provider_config.http.deref().clone();
tracing::info!(chain=%chain_id, rpc_url=%rpc_url, rate_limit=?provider_config.rate_limit, "Using HTTP transport");
```

Most hosted RPC providers put the API key in the URL — as a path segment (`https://host/v2/<key>`), a query string (`?apikey=`), or userinfo (`https://user:token@host`). All three end up verbatim in the container log on every start, and container logs are routinely shipped to log aggregators, pasted into issues, and kept in rotated files with broader read permissions than the env file the key came from.

## Ask

Log the URL with userinfo, query string and any path segments beyond the first redacted — e.g. `https://host/<redacted>` — or log only the host. A small helper that parses the URL and prints `scheme://host[:port]` covers the three shapes above. Same for any other place a provider URL is logged or included in an error message.

## Why it matters

The only thing an operator can do today is avoid keyed URLs (not possible with most providers) or scrub logs after the fact. A one-line redaction at the source fixes it for every deployment.

title: eip155 settle: add fee-cap headroom or retry once on "fee cap less than base fee" — currently surfaces as unexpected_error under a base-fee spike
body:
## Summary

Under a base-fee spike, `POST /settle` fails with the node's error passed through as `unexpected_error`:

```
server returned an error response: error code -32000: failed to calculate effective gas tip: fee cap less than base fee
```

The transaction's `maxFeePerGas` was chosen a moment before broadcast and the next block's base fee moved above it. A retry a few seconds later succeeds. Observed on Celo mainnet (`eip155:42220`) during a 1,005-settlement Permit2 soak: 2 of 1,005 settlements failed this way, both transient.

## Where

`crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/chain/provider.rs` composes alloy's `GasFiller` into the provider (`JoinFill<GasFiller, …>`), so fees are filled from the node's estimate at fill time, and `v2_eip155_exact/facilitator/permit2.rs` / `eip3009.rs` call `send_transaction` once with whatever was filled. There is no headroom over the estimated base fee and no retry on this specific rejection.

## Ask

Either or both:

1. Add headroom when filling `maxFeePerGas` (e.g. `2 × baseFee + priorityFee`, which is what most wallets do), so a one-block base-fee move does not invalidate the transaction.
2. On `-32000 … fee cap less than base fee`, re-fill fees against the latest block and resend once, before surfacing the error.

Separately from the fix: the error is transient by nature, so a facilitator could classify it as retryable (`Retry-After`) rather than `unexpected_error`. We do that in the gateway in front of our facilitator today; doing it in the facilitator would help every deployment.

## Environment

`ghcr.io/x402-rs/x402-facilitator` at digest `sha256:8eb27a73…` (2.0.1, rev `de2e55bc`), Celo mainnet via a standard JSON-RPC provider, EIP-1559.

title: feat(x402-types): add arbitrum, bnb, and pulsechain to KNOWN_NETWORKS
body:
## What

Adds three EVM entries to `KNOWN_NETWORKS` in `crates/x402-types/src/networks.rs`:

| name | CAIP-2 chain id |
| --- | --- |
| `arbitrum` | `eip155:42161` |
| `bnb` | `eip155:56` |
| `pulsechain` | `eip155:369` |

…along with the module-doc network list, the two network counts in that doc, and the three
existing unit tests. The shape follows 940a6f9 (`add Radius Network and Radius Testnet`), which is
the most recent addition to this table.

## Why

x402 v2 carries the chain as a CAIP-2 id in the payload, so routing parses it directly and any
chain id works with config alone. x402 v1 carries a network *name*, and routing resolves it via
`ChainId::from_network_name()` → `NAME_TO_CHAIN_ID` → the `KNOWN_NETWORKS` static array. A name
that is not in that array returns `None`, and the request is rejected as `UnsupportedScheme`.
Config cannot add a name.

The result is that these three chains are fully routable under v2 today but unreachable from a v1
client purely for want of a table entry.

We run a self-hosted x402-rs facilitator that serves PulseChain (`eip155:369`) alongside Arbitrum
and BNB, and its `/supported` output shows the asymmetry directly — `eip155:369`, `eip155:42161`
and `eip155:56` are advertised for v2, while the only v1 names it can advertise are `base` and
`polygon`: <https://402.wick.pics/supported>. With this patch a v1 client can address those chains
by name.

## On the names

v1 network names are a de-facto registry rather than a standard, so the choice is worth stating:

- `arbitrum` — already answered by at least one other public facilitator, so this
  aligns x402-rs with existing v1 client expectations rather than minting a name.
- `bnb` and `pulsechain` — the short, lowercase, common chain name, matching the convention the
  rest of the array already uses (`base`, `polygon`, `celo`, `peaq`, `iotex`).

Happy to rename any of them if you would prefer a different form (`bsc`, `bnb-smart-chain`,
`arbitrum-one`); the point of the PR is the resolution, not the spelling.

## Scope

Data only. Deliberately **not** included:

- No `KnownNetworkEip155` trait methods for these chains, and no `USDC`/`SBC` token deployment
  entries in `x402-chain-eip155`. Asset availability is a separate question from name resolution,
  and I did not want the PR to imply a token deployment claim. (The Radius change likewise listed
  its networks in the `x402-types` module doc without adding `KnownNetworkEip155` methods, so the
  doc edit here follows that precedent.)
- No `CHANGELOG.md` entry: the file has no `Unreleased` section (latest heading is `## [2.0.0]`),
  so there is no obvious place to put one. Glad to add an entry wherever you would like it.

## Verification

- Chain ids checked against live `eth_chainId`: Arbitrum One `0xa4b1` (42161), BNB Smart Chain
  `0x38` (56), PulseChain `0x171` (369).
- `cargo fmt -p x402-types -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo test -p x402-types --lib networks` — passes.

title: x402-reqwest signs a fresh payment on every 402 — no idempotency key against duplicate settlement on retry
body:
## `x402-reqwest` middleware signs a fresh payment on every 402 — no idempotency key against duplicate settlement on retry

Reading `crates/x402-reqwest/src/client.rs`, `X402Client::handle` (the `rqm::Middleware` impl, roughly lines 245-278) does: clone the outgoing request (`req.try_clone()`), run it, and if the response status is `PAYMENT_REQUIRED`, call `self.make_payment_headers(res)` — which signs a brand-new payment payload via the registered scheme client — then retries the cloned request with the new payment header attached via `run_next`.

There's no state carried across calls to `handle`: no cache of "this request body/URL already got a signed payment," and no idempotency key sent to the resource server or facilitator alongside the payment payload. That means:

- If the *paid* retry (the request in `run_next(next, retry, extensions)`) itself times out or the connection drops after the facilitator/resource server already settled on-chain, and something upstream of this middleware (a caller's own retry wrapper, `reqwest-retry`'s `RetryTransientMiddleware` stacked on top, etc.) resends the same logical request, `handle` runs again from scratch: sees a fresh 402 (or possibly succeeds against a server that already has state, depending on server behavior), and signs and attaches a *second* independent payment authorization for what is logically one purchase.
- Nothing in this crate gives a resource server or facilitator a way to recognize the retry as the same intent and return the original settlement instead of processing a new one.

This is the same failure shape `x402-foundation/x402`'s own tracker has open under #808 ("Add configurable idempotency keys for paid requests to prevent accidental double-charging") and #832 (client-side retry/idempotency helper) — worth noting since x402-reqwest is one of the reference client crates that'd consume whatever spec-level primitive lands there, but there's no interim mitigation in this crate's retry path today.

We hit the identical class of bug on the server side (client times out waiting on our response, retries, and — without a guard — pays twice) and shipped a fix live since 2026-08-01: an opt-in `Idempotency-Key` header that keys a short-TTL cache of the *original* result, so a retry with the same key returns the original response with no second settlement. No key sent, no behavior change — it's additive. `https://scvd.store` documents the header contract if useful as a concrete reference while the spec-level primitive in #808/#832 is still being worked out.

For x402-reqwest, the natural spot looks like: an optional field on `X402Client` (or a builder option) that lets a caller supply a stable request identifier, threaded as a header alongside `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`/`X-Payment` on the retried request, and/or caching the signed payload keyed by request-body digest for a short window so a caller-level retry replays the same payment instead of signing a new one. Happy to sketch a PR if that's a useful shape — mostly wanted to flag the gap since the middleware currently has no way to distinguish "first attempt" from "retry of the same logical call."

title: fix(eip155): return 4xx for a replayed ERC-3009 authorization
body:
## Motivation

A client retrying a nonce it already spent gets `execution reverted: FiatTokenV2: authorization is used or canceled` out of `eth_estimateGas`. That arrived as `Eip155ExactError::Transport`, mapped to `OnchainFailure`, and left `/verify` and `/settle` answering **500** with `unexpected_error`.

The payload can never succeed. Nothing the facilitator does changes the outcome, so it is a client error, and 500 makes every duplicate submission look like a facilitator fault to anything watching error rates. `insufficient_funds` and `invalid_payment_expired` already return 400 for the same class of problem.

Reproduced against mainnet on 2026-08-24:

```
[settle first]  200  {"success":true,"transaction":"0x62a110e0..."}
[settle replay] 500  {"errorReason":"unexpected_error",
                      "errorMessage":"execution reverted: FiatTokenV2: authorization is used or canceled"}
```

## Modifications

**`v1_eip155_exact/facilitator.rs`**

- `From<Eip155ExactError> for X402SchemeFacilitatorError` inspects `Transport` and `ContractCall` for an ERC-3009 replay revert and maps it to `PaymentVerificationError::TransactionSimulation`.
- Matching is on the reason substring, not the whole message, because the prefix is the token contract's own name and differs between deployments. `REPLAYED_AUTHORIZATION_REVERTS` also carries the older FiatTokenV2 wording that omits "or canceled".
- Everything else is untouched: unrelated reverts, reverted receipts, pending-transaction errors and real transport failures all still return 500.

Covers both v1 and v2 exact, since `v2_eip155_exact` reuses `Eip155ExactError`.

## Result

- `/verify` and `/settle` answer **400** with `transaction_simulation` for a spent authorization.
- A duplicate submission no longer counts against settlement error rate.
- 6 new unit tests, including that a real transport failure and an unrelated revert both stay `unexpected_error`.

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo test -p x402-chain-eip155 --features facilitator` are clean.

## Before merge

Consumers pin this repo by rev. `monad-x402` needs `facilitator/Cargo.toml` bumped off `f2bf161` once this lands, or the fix does not ship.

title: fix(solana,aptos): reject unsigned payments at /verify
body:
## Summary

`Facilitator::verify` is documented to include signature validity. The EVM exact adapter does that. The Solana and Aptos exact adapters did not.

Solana `/verify` simulated with `sig_verify: false` and never checked the payer signature. Settle only rejected the all-zero default signature via `is_fully_signed`, so a garbage non-zero signature still passed verify. Aptos `/verify` only checked that the Ed25519 public key derived to the claimed sender, then simulated with `NoAccountAuthenticator`.

x402-axum's default paygate (`settle_before_execution: false`) runs the inner handler after a successful verify and before settle. A structurally valid unsigned or forged Solana/Aptos payment could therefore execute the protected handler even though settlement cannot succeed.

## Change

- Solana (V1 and V2 share `verify_transaction`): require a non-default, cryptographically valid signature from every required signer other than the facilitator fee payer.
- Aptos: require an Ed25519 sender authenticator whose signature verifies over the raw transaction, or the fee-payer wrapped message.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p x402-chain-solana --features facilitator --lib` (13 passed, including default-sig and forged-sig refusals)
- [x] `cargo test -p x402-chain-aptos --features facilitator --lib` (34 passed, including forged-sig, pubkey mismatch, `NoAccountAuthenticator`, and fee-payer message binding)

title: fix(eip155): check contract dependencies per payment path
body:
## Summary

- remove unconditional EVM contract checks from provider initialization
- validate Permit2 and proxy deployments only for Permit2 payment paths
- validate the EIP-6492 Validator and Multicall3 only when processing EIP-6492 signatures
- preserve zero-value `upto` settlements without unnecessary RPC calls
- add mock-provider tests for deployed and missing contract dependencies

## Motivation

`Eip155ChainProvider::from_config` previously required the EIP-6492
Validator, Permit2, and the Exact Permit2 Proxy to be deployed before the
provider could start.

These dependencies are payment-path specific:

- EIP-3009 with EOA or EIP-1271 does not require Permit2 or the Validator
- Exact Permit2 requires Permit2 and the Exact Proxy
- Upto Permit2 requires Permit2 and the Upto Proxy
- EIP-6492 verification requires the Validator and Multicall3
- counterfactual wallet settlement requires Multicall3 only when the wallet
  has not yet been deployed

The previous startup check prevented otherwise supported EVM payment paths
from running on chains missing unrelated contracts. It also checked the Exact
Proxy globally while not checking the Upto Proxy.

This change aligns provider startup behavior with the upstream x402
implementation, where contract dependencies are evaluated only when the
corresponding payment path is used.

## Behavior
- provider initialization now depends only on RPC and signer configuration
- missing contracts fail only the affected verify or settle request
- EOA and EIP-1271 EIP-3009 payments no longer depend on Permit2 or the
  EIP-6492 Validator
- EIP-6492 requests continue to fail closed when their required contracts are
  unavailable
- EIP-2612 extension payloads are validated before contract RPC checks

title: Proposal: Optional decision verification layer (tower middleware) between verify and settle
body:
# Proposal: Optional decision verification layer (tower middleware) between verify and settle

## Context

x402.rs verifies that payments are cryptographically valid and settles them on-chain. But there's a gap between "this payment is authorized" and "this payment is well-justified."

An agent can produce a perfectly valid payment signature for a service it doesn't need, at a price it shouldn't accept, based on reasoning that wouldn't survive scrutiny. The facilitator currently has no opinion on decision quality — by design.

## Proposal

A `tower::Layer` that optionally sits between the verify and settle stages in the Axum middleware pipeline. It intercepts the payment context after signature verification passes and evaluates whether the agent's *decision to pay* is justified, not just authorized.

```
Request → x402-axum verify → [decision-verification layer] → settle → Response
```

If the decision check fails (confidence below threshold), the layer returns a `402` with an extended header indicating *why* settlement was held — not a payment failure, but a reasoning quality hold.

## Sketch

```rust
use tower::Layer;

pub struct DecisionVerificationLayer {
    /// Confidence threshold (0.0 - 1.0). Below this → hold settlement.
    threshold: f64,
    /// Stake level affects scrutiny depth
    stake_level: StakeLevel,
}

pub enum StakeLevel {
    Micro,   // < $5, threshold 0.40, material defects only
    Low,     // < $50, threshold 0.50
    Medium,  // < $500, threshold 0.60
    High,    // < $5000, threshold 0.75
    Critical, // > $5000, threshold 0.85, full adversarial
}

pub enum VerificationVerdict {
    Allow { confidence: f64 },
    Hold { confidence: f64, reason: String },
}
```

The layer would call an external verification service (or run locally) that evaluates the payment context — amount, payee, description, and any available agent reasoning — against a multi-model adversarial check.

## Why this fits x402.rs architecture

- x402-axum already uses tower middleware for payment gating
- The verification layer would be a standard `tower::Layer` — opt-in, composable
- Servers that don't want it skip it. Servers that want decision quality checks add one line
- No changes to the core facilitator logic

## Related work

We built a TypeScript equivalent as a `beforeSettle` hook for the `@x402/core` facilitator:
- https://github.com/ThoughtProof/pot-x402
- Uses the same pattern: verify payment → verify decision → settle

Your Machinomy work showed you've been thinking about HTTP micropayments longer than almost anyone. Curious whether you see decision-quality verification as a useful addition to the facilitator stack, or whether you'd keep the facilitator strictly payment-focused and push verification to a separate layer.

## Not asking for

- Not asking to merge anything
- Not proposing changes to the core protocol
- Interested in whether this is a useful direction and whether you'd review a draft implementation

title: upto scheme always settles for max authorized amount
body:
## The bug

`upto` currently settles for the full max every time. The facilitator code handles variable amounts correctly — `assert_offchain_valid_settle()` in `v2_eip155_upto/facilitator/permit2.rs:128` reads `payment_requirements.amount` from the request and settles for exactly that. But the `Paygate` middleware passes the original `VerifyRequest` raw JSON unchanged to `settle()`. Since `SettleRequest = VerifyRequest` (type alias), `payment_requirements.amount` still contains the authorized max, not the actual consumption.

**Result:** upto settles for the full max every time. Functionally identical to `exact` with higher gas costs (Permit2 vs direct transfer).

## Current flow (settle-after-execution)

```
1. Client sends Payment-Signature with max=$5.00 USDC authorization
2. Paygate extracts payment header → verify_request (amount=5000000)
3. Paygate calls facilitator.verify(&verify_request) → OK
4. Paygate calls inner handler → response (consumed $2.35 worth)
5. Paygate calls facilitator.settle(&verify_request) → settles for $5.00
   ^^ verify_request still has amount=5000000, not 2350000
```

The handler runs, produces a response, but has no mechanism to tell the middleware what was actually consumed. The middleware has no way to know — so it settles the only amount it has, which is the authorized max.

## Proposed fix

A typed parallel channel: `UptoSettleAmount(U256)` as a response extension, consumed by the middleware to build a `SettleContext` that carries the actual settlement amount alongside the immutable `VerifyRequest`.

```rust
/// Insert into response extensions to report actual consumption for upto settlement.
/// U256 from alloy-primitives — atomic units, same denomination as paymentRequirements.amount.
pub struct UptoSettleAmount(pub U256);

/// Parallel channel from middleware to facilitator. VerifyRequest is never modified.
pub struct SettleContext {
    pub settle_amount: Option<UptoSettleAmount>,
    pub scheme: PaymentScheme,
}
```

Middleware pseudocode after handler returns:

```rust
let ctx = build_settle_context(scheme, response.extensions(), max_authorized)?;
// exact: ignores extension, settles full amount
// upto + extension: validates amount <= max, builds typed context
// upto + no extension: returns Error (handler forgot to report consumption)

let settlement = facilitator.settle_with_context(&verify_request, &ctx).await?;
let header = settlement_succeeded(&settlement)?; // fix for #65
```

The raw `VerifyRequest` is passed to the facilitator unchanged. The `SettleContext` carries the typed override separately.

## Configuration guard

`validate_paygate_config()` runs at startup and rejects `upto` + `settle_before_execution = true`. When settle-before runs, the handler hasn't executed yet — there is no consumption to report. This is a configuration error, not a runtime case.

## Settlement validation

`settlement_succeeded()` checks the `success` field in the scheme-specific response before returning the header. If `success: false`, returns an error rather than a 200 with a failed payment header. This bundles the fix for #65.

## Why this approach

JSON rewriting (the obvious alternative) is explicitly rejected:
- `VerifyRequest` is `Box<RawValue>` — the type signals "preserve this exactly"
- Round-trip through `serde_json::Value` reorders fields, breaks any signature covering field order
- String manipulation on raw JSON is fragile
- Malformed input (non-numeric amount string) becomes a runtime panic risk

The typed parallel channel keeps the immutable invariant of `VerifyRequest` while giving the middleware a clean, validated amount to work with. Malformed input is impossible — `U256::from(cost_atomic)` either compiles or it doesn't.

Happy to submit a PR for this — have a working prototype with the typed design. Would appreciate feedback on the approach, especially how `SettleContext` should thread through the `Facilitator` → `X402SchemeFacilitator` trait hierarchy.

## Related

- Spec: coinbase/x402 PR #1074 (`scheme_upto.md`, `scheme_upto_evm.md`)
- Settlement validation: #65
- EIP-2612 upto alternative: #60 (conflicting, likely stale)
- Dynamic pricing hooks: #40 (related, composes with this fix)

body:
## Summary

Adds the EIP-155 batch-settlement facilitator implementation for x402-rs.

This implements Rust facilitator-side support for the `batch-settlement` scheme, covering verification and settlement flows described by the x402 batch-settlement docs and the Go facilitator reference.

References:

- https://docs.x402.org/schemes/batch-settlement
- https://www.x402.org/writing/x402-batch-settlement
- https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/tree/main/examples/go/facilitator/batch-settlement

## Implementation

The facilitator now supports:

- Deposit verification and settlement for ERC-3009 deposits.
- Deposit verification and settlement for canonical Permit2 prior-allowance deposits.
- Voucher verification against channel state, including ECDSA and EIP-1271 signature paths.
- Claim settlement with receiver-authorizer signatures.
- Receiver settlement through `settle(receiver, token)`.
- Client refund verification and enriched refund settlement.
- Channel state extras for verify, settle, and corrective responses.
- Batch-settlement error codes and response serialization.

## Verification Behavior

- Deposit `/verify` rejects malformed zero or uint128-overflow deposit amounts.
- Deposit `/verify` validates the deposit authorization, voucher, channel config, channel state, payer balance, and simulates the deposit call.
- Deposit `/verify` returns projected post-deposit channel state, matching the Go reference.
- Voucher and refund verification return corrective channel/voucher state where applicable.
- Enriched refund payloads are rejected on `/verify`; client refund payloads are accepted.

## Settlement Behavior

- Deposit `/settle` submits the deposit transaction and returns channel state that is resilient to stale RPC reads.
- Claim `/settle` simulates before submitting claim transactions.
- Receiver `settle(receiver, token)` validates receiver/token, simulates, submits the settlement transaction, and reports the settled event amount when present.
- Refund `/settle` checks channel nonce/state, simulates direct refund or refund+claim multicall, reports actual refund, and allows other-channel claims in the multicall while only counting same-channel claims for refund availability.

## Security / Correctness Notes

- ERC-3009 and Permit2 signatures are verified during `/verify` before settlement.
- Permit2 support binds owner, spender, token, amount, witness, deadline, and prior allowance.
- Integer narrowing from `uint256` to `uint128` is checked before ABI calls.
- Refund nonce and channel state are checked before submitting refund settlement.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p x402-chain-eip155 --features facilitator`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `git diff --check`

# Add v2-eip155-upto Payment Scheme with TypeScript Integration Example

## Overview

This PR introduces the **`v2-eip155-upto` payment scheme** for batched EVM payments using EIP-2612 permits. Unlike the exact scheme (one payment = one transaction), the upto scheme enables **multiple payments under a single permit authorization**, reducing on-chain costs by **80%+** for frequent small transactions.
---

## Upto Scheme Implementation

**Core Implementation:**
- `src/scheme/v2_eip155_upto/mod.rs` - Verification and settlement logic
- `src/scheme/v2_eip155_upto/types.rs` - Type definitions
- `src/scheme/v2_eip155_upto/client.rs` - Test utilities
- `src/scheme/mod.rs` - Scheme registration

**Key Features:**
-  Batched payments (multiple requests, single settlement)
-  EIP-2612 permit-based authorization (`permit()` + `transferFrom()`)
-  EOA and EIP-1271 smart wallet signatures
-  Automatic nonce/allowance management
-  Comprehensive test coverage (37 tests)

**How it works:**
1. Client creates EIP-2612 permit with spending cap (e.g., $0.01 for 10×$0.001 payments)
2. Client reuses same permit for multiple API calls (cached, no new signatures)
3. Facilitator verifies each payment off-chain (no gas cost)
4. Settlement batches all payments into one on-chain transaction

**Documentation:** See [`upto_scheme.md`](upto_scheme.md) (1,490 lines) for complete technical deep-dive including:
- Architecture and payment flow
- Verification/settlement logic with code examples
- Security considerations and best practices
- Complete transaction flow walkthrough (client → server → facilitator → blockchain)
- API reference and troubleshooting guide

---

## Example Integration Test

**Location:** `examples/upto-rust-ts-test/`

Demonstrates production-ready **hybrid architecture**:
- **Rust facilitator** (x402-rs) - Payment verification and settlement
- **TypeScript client** ([`@daydreamsai/facilitator/client`](https://github.com/daydreamsai/facilitator)) - Permit creation and caching
- **TypeScript middleware** ([`@daydreamsai/facilitator/express`](https://github.com/daydreamsai/facilitator)) - Payment handling and session tracking

**Test Results (Polygon Mainnet - Jan 2026):**
```
API Calls: 3/3 successful
 Total Cost: 0.003 USDC (3 × 0.001 USDC)
 Batching: All 3 calls reused same permit
 Settlement: Auto-triggered at $0.003 threshold
 Transactions: 2 on-chain (1 permit + 1 settlement)
  Total Time: 41.2s
 Network: Polygon Mainnet (eip155:137)
```

**Test demonstrates:**
- Permit creation and caching (first call)
- Permit reuse for batched payments (subsequent calls)
- Threshold-based auto-settlement ($0.003 accumulated)
- Single settlement transaction for all payments

**Quick Start:**
```bash
cd examples/upto-rust-ts-test
pnpm install && pnpm run server  # Terminal 1
pnpm run client                   # Terminal 2
```

**Documentation:**
- [`examples/upto-rust-ts-test/README.md`](examples/upto-rust-ts-test/README.md) - Setup and usage
- [`examples/upto-rust-ts-test/QUICK_START_TS_RUST.md`](examples/upto-rust-ts-test/QUICK_START_TS_RUST.md) - Quick reference
- [`examples/upto-rust-ts-test/UPTO_TS_INTEGRATION_ANALYSIS.md`](examples/upto-rust-ts-test/UPTO_TS_INTEGRATION_ANALYSIS.md) - Technical analysis

---

## References

**Source Repositories:**
- **TypeScript Libraries:** [daydreamsai/facilitator](https://github.com/daydreamsai/facilitator) - Client, middleware, and upto module
- **Rust Facilitator:** [x402-rs/x402-rs](https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs) - This repository

**Key Standards:**
- [EIP-2612](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612) - Permit extension for ERC-20
- [EIP-712](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712) - Typed structured data hashing
- [EIP-1271](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1271) - Smart wallet signature validation

---

## Configuration

Add to `config.json`:
```json
{
  "schemes": [{
    "id": "v2-eip155-upto",
    "chains": "eip155:*",
    "enabled": true
  }]
}
```

**Important:** Use only **one signer** to ensure permit spender matches settlement signer.

---

## 🔄 Comparison: Upto vs Exact

| Feature | Upto | Exact |
|---------|------|-------|
| **Authorization** | EIP-2612 permit | ERC-3009 transferWithAuthorization |
| **Payments per signature** | Multiple | One |
| **Gas cost (10 payments)** | 2 transactions | 10 transactions |
| **Best for** | Frequent small payments | One-time large payments |

---

##  Checklist

- [x] Implementation complete with 37 comprehensive tests
- [x] Technical documentation (1,490 lines)
- [x] Production-tested integration example
- [x] Verified on Polygon Mainnet with real transactions
- [x] Compatible with TypeScript x402 ecosystem
- [x] No breaking changes to existing schemes

---

## Migration & Impact

**For existing facilitators:** No breaking changes. Opt-in via configuration.

**Use cases:**
- API rate limiting / metered access
- Subscription services
- Micro-transactions
- Pay-per-use models

**Performance benefits:**
- 80%+ reduction in on-chain transactions
- Lower gas costs for users
- Better UX (cached permits, fewer wallet interactions)

title: Validate accepted.pay_to against payment_requirements.pay_to in v2_eip155_upto
body:
Hi, I noticed a potential recipient-binding gap in the V2 EIP-155 `upto` Permit2 facilitator path.

In `crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/v2_eip155_upto/facilitator/permit2.rs`, `assert_offchain_valid` validates several fields across the embedded `payment_payload.accepted`, the signed Permit2 authorization, and `payment_requirements`:

- `accepted.network == payment_requirements.network`
- `accepted.asset == payment_requirements.asset`
- `authorization.spender == UPTO_PERMIT2_PROXY_ADDRESS`
- `authorization.witness.to == accepted.pay_to`
- `authorization.permitted.token == accepted.asset`

However, I do not see a corresponding check that `accepted.pay_to == payment_requirements.pay_to`. The recipient is therefore bound to the client-embedded `accepted.pay_to`, but not directly to the server/facilitator-provided `payment_requirements.pay_to`.

This matters because settlement later rebuilds the Permit2 witness from the payment payload and passes it into `x402UptoPermit2Proxy::settle(...)`. In contrast, the V2 exact EIP-3009 path appears to call `assert_requirements_match(accepted, payment_requirements)` before validating the authorization, which enforces full congruence between the embedded accepted terms and the server requirements.

Relevant current code paths:

- `assert_offchain_valid`: https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/980ad88cc2639fd165476212750d3786bfd1c600/crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/v2_eip155_upto/facilitator/permit2.rs#L193-L236
- `assert_offchain_valid_settle`: https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/980ad88cc2639fd165476212750d3786bfd1c600/crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/v2_eip155_upto/facilitator/permit2.rs#L172-L190
- settlement using `witness`: https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/980ad88cc2639fd165476212750d3786bfd1c600/crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/v2_eip155_upto/facilitator/permit2.rs#L376-L407
- exact V2 path with full requirements match: https://github.com/x402-rs/x402-rs/blob/980ad88cc2639fd165476212750d3786bfd1c600/crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/v2_eip155_exact/facilitator/eip3009.rs#L24-L30

Suggested direction:

- add an explicit `accepted.pay_to == payment_requirements.pay_to` check in `assert_offchain_valid`, or
- consider a full `accepted == payment_requirements` congruence check for the `upto` path if that matches the intended V2 invariant, similar to the exact path
- add a regression test where `accepted.network` and `accepted.asset` match `payment_requirements`, but `accepted.pay_to` differs

One caveat: the `x402-axum` paygate appears to match `payment_payload.accepted` against server-side `accepts` before constructing a verify request, which may mitigate this for callers using that layer. Still, enforcing the invariant inside the scheme-level facilitator would make this path safer for direct facilitator usage and future integrations.

Thanks for maintaining this implementation.

title: batch-settlement (V2, EVM): reference implementation + EIP-712 vectors — proposal
body:
# Proposal: `batch-settlement` (V2, EVM) for x402-rs

## Context

`x402-rs` is the mature general Rust x402 implementation: `exact` V2
across chains, a facilitator, axum/reqwest middleware. The roadmap
lists the deferred / `batch-settlement` family as **Planned**. It is
also absent from `x402-core`. So there is currently no Rust
implementation of `batch-settlement`.

While measuring the latency cost of x402-gated LLM serving, I built a
spec-pinned `batch-settlement` (V2, EVM) cryptographic core and would
like to contribute it, aligned to your scheme architecture.

## Why batch-settlement matters here (motivation, measured)

Same harness, Base Sepolia, overhead = total − upstream:

- `exact`, synchronous verify+settle: p99 overhead ≈ 2.4 s — ~490×
  over a 5 ms target; the per-request facilitator round trips and
  on-chain settle dominate.
- `batch-settlement`, steady-state voucher (release build): p99
  overhead ≈ 0.39 ms — no facilitator round trip, no chain on the hot
  path, value committed once on-chain via the channel deposit.

For agent / pay-per-call workloads this is the difference between
unusable and usable. It is the strongest argument for prioritising the
scheme.

## What I have, precisely

- EIP-712 `ChannelConfig → channelId`, `Voucher` digest, secp256k1
  signer recovery, and the server-authored `claim` / `settle`
  payloads.
- **Golden tests byte-exact against `viem`** (the library the official
  client SDK signs with): the verbatim Base64 vectors from the x402
  spec decode and reproduce `channelId`, the voucher digest and signer
  recovery exactly. These vectors are reusable as conformance tests
  regardless of how the scheme is structured here.
- A reference router that exercises the hot path; the `claim` leg has
  executed on-chain against the hosted facilitator.

## How it could fit x402-rs

Issue-first, to align with your design before any PR:

- A `v2-eip155-batch-settlement` handler implementing
  `X402SchemeFacilitator` (verify/settle/supported) in
  `x402-chain-eip155`, registered via `SchemeBlueprints`.
- The client side via `X402SchemeClient` / `PaymentCandidate`.
- The EIP-712 vectors contributed as conformance tests in
  `x402-types` or the chain crate.

I would adapt the core to your `X402SchemeId` /
`X402SchemeFacilitatorBuilder` model rather than drop in a parallel
abstraction.

## Honest scope / maturity

In: the cryptographic core, voucher verification, server-authored
`claim`/`settle`. Proven by golden vectors and an on-chain `claim`.

Not done: the channel-lifecycle long-tail — cooperative refund,
recovery-after-state-loss, withdrawal monitoring, multi-policy claim
strategies. The full escrow → recipient closure was demonstrated only
partially (the `claim` leg landed on-chain; the `settle` leg and
cross-restart state reconciliation are not fully closed). I am
flagging this so the maturity is clear up front.

Reference and vectors:
https://github.com/Adelagric/x402-batch-settlement
