title: fix(paygate): validate SettleResponse.success before serving protected resources
body:
## Summary

Fixes #65 — `settlement_to_header()` serializes `SettleResponse` into the payment header without checking the `success` field. When a facilitator returns HTTP 200 with `{ "success": false }`, the paygate serves the protected resource despite failed on-chain settlement.

This is a parity gap with the official TypeScript implementation, which explicitly checks `!settleResponse.success` and returns 402 on failure.

## Changes

**`crates/x402-axum/src/paygate.rs`**

Add `validate_settlement()` that inspects the `success` field on `SettleResponse.0` (the inner `serde_json::Value`). Called in both execution paths of `handle_request_fallible`, between `settle_payment()` and `settlement_to_header()`:

```rust
let settlement = self.settle_payment(&verify_request).await?;
validate_settlement(&settlement)?;
let header_value = settlement_to_header(settlement)?;
```

### Fail-safe behavior

| `success` value | Result |
|---|---|
| `true` (bool) | `Ok(())` — proceed to serve resource |
| `false` (bool) | `Err` with `errorReason` extracted if available |
| Missing field | `Err` — non-compliant facilitator response |
| Non-boolean (`"true"`, `1`) | `Err` — malformed per spec |

### Design decisions

- **No changes to `SettleResponse` type.** It stays `pub struct SettleResponse(pub serde_json::Value)` — the check reads the inner Value without adding typed fields. Keeps the change minimal and avoids downstream type breakage.
- **`PaygateError::Settlement` reused.** The existing variant already handles settlement failures and maps to the right HTTP response (402). No new error variant needed.
- **Missing `success` → error, not pass-through.** Fail-safe. A conforming facilitator always includes this field; absence indicates a broken or non-compliant response.

## Impact

| Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `settle_before_execution` | **High** — zero-balance wallets access resources | Settlement failure → `PaygateError::Settlement` → 402 |
| verify-first (default) | **Low** — verify catches most cases, narrow race window | Race window closed — both verify and settle must succeed |

## Tests

7 new unit tests in `paygate::tests`:

- `validate_settlement_success_true` — happy path
- `validate_settlement_success_false_with_reason` — extracts `errorReason`
- `validate_settlement_success_false_no_reason` — falls back to "unknown"
- `validate_settlement_missing_success_field` — fail-safe
- `validate_settlement_success_is_string` — rejects `"true"`
- `validate_settlement_success_is_number` — rejects `1`
- `validate_settlement_empty_object` — fail-safe

All 12 tests pass (`cargo test -p x402-axum`).

## Note

There is a pre-existing clippy warning on `main` (`derivable_impls` for `ResourceInfoBuilder::Default`) unrelated to this change.

title: feat: Implement V2 EIP-155 "upto" payment scheme with Permit2 support
body:
This PR implements the V2 EIP-155 "upto" payment scheme as per [draft spec](https://github.com/coinbase/x402/pull/1074), enabling usage-based payments where clients authorize a maximum amount and servers settle for the actual amount consumed. This is ideal for variable-cost resources like LLM token generation, bandwidth metering, or time-based access.

⚠️ **Work In Progress**: This implementation includes Rust facilitator and TypeScript client/server support, but **does not yet include Axum server integration**. The upto scheme is [not yet production-ready](https://github.com/coinbase/x402/pull/1089#issuecomment-3874294728).

## Key Features
- **Variable Settlement**: Client signs a maximum amount, server settles actual usage (can be ≤ max)
- **Permit2 Only**: Uses Uniswap's Permit2 exclusively (EIP-3009 requires exact amounts)
- **Zero Settlement**: Supports $0 settlements without on-chain transactions
- **Usage-Based Pricing**: Perfect for LLM tokens, bandwidth, compute metering

## Changes
- Added `v2_eip155_upto` module to eip155 chain crate with client and facilitator support
- Implemented Permit2-based payment flow with witness pattern for receiver security
- Added `X402UptoPermit2Proxy` contract ABI (219 lines)
- Added TypeScript client and server implementations for protocol compliance (while the reference SDK does not have it)
- Created new test suites:
  - `v2-eip155-upto-ts-rs-rs.test.ts` - TS client, Rust facilitator, Rust settlement
  - `v2-eip155-upto-ts-ts-rs.test.ts` - TS client, TS server, Rust facilitator

### Configuration
- Updated facilitator config example with upto scheme support
- Integrated upto scheme into facilitator scheme registry

## Differences from "exact" Scheme
- `amount` represents **maximum** authorized (not exact)
- Actual settled amount can be less than or equal to maximum
- Only Permit2 supported (no EIP-3009)
- Settlement can be $0 (no transaction needed)

## Use Cases
- LLM token generation (charge per token generated)
- Bandwidth metering (pay per byte transferred)  
- Dynamic compute pricing (charge based on resources consumed)
- Any variable-cost resource with upfront authorization

## Known Limitations
- ❌ **No Axum server support yet** - The `x402-axum` crate does not yet support the upto scheme
- ❌ **Not production-ready** - Additional integration work needed
- ✅ Rust facilitator implementation complete
- ✅ TypeScript client/server implementations complete
- ✅ Protocol compliance tests passing

## Security Considerations
- Clients must trust servers to charge fair amounts based on actual usage
- Maximum amount authorization limits exposure
- Permit2 nonce mechanism prevents signature reuse
- Time constraints (`deadline`, `validAfter`) limit authorization lifetime

title: V1 VerifyRequest deserialization fails on /verify endpoint
body:
## Description

The `/verify` endpoint returns a 400 error when receiving any V1-formatted `VerifyRequest` in the body. The Serde untagged enum `VerifyRequestEnvelope` cannot deserialize any V1 JSON structure.

**Error:**
```
Failed to deserialize VerifyRequest: data did not match any variant of untagged enum VerifyRequestEnvelope
```

## Reproduction

```bash
# V2 via payment-signature header — WORKS
curl -X POST https://facilitator.ultravioletadao.xyz/verify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "payment-signature: <base64-encoded-v2-payload>" \
  -d '{}'
# Response: 200 {"isValid":true,"payer":"0x377..."}

# V1 body format — FAILS
curl -X POST https://facilitator.ultravioletadao.xyz/verify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"x402Version":1,"scheme":"exact","network":"avalanche-fuji","payload":{"signature":"0x...","authorization":{"from":"0x...","to":"0x...","value":"1000","validAfter":"0","validBefore":"...","nonce":"0x..."}}}'
# Response: 400 "Failed to deserialize VerifyRequest: data did not match any variant of untagged enum VerifyRequestEnvelope"
```

## Context

- **Facilitator**: `https://facilitator.ultravioletadao.xyz` (appears to be running x402-rs)
- **Network**: Avalanche Fuji (`eip155:43113`)
- **V2 works perfectly**: Both `/verify` and `/settle` succeed when the payload is sent via `payment-signature` header
- **V1 never works**: We tested multiple V1 JSON structures (with and without `paymentPayload` wrapper, `paymentRequirements` field, etc.) — all fail with the same Serde error

## Impact

Services that send V1-formatted payloads in the body (like SnowRail's middleware) cannot verify payments through the facilitator, even though the underlying EIP-712 signatures are valid.

We confirmed the signatures are valid by:
1. Local verification with `viem.verifyTypedData()` → `true`
2. V2 verification via `payment-signature` header → `{"isValid":true}`
3. 7 successful on-chain settlements via `/settle` with the same signatures

## Expected Behavior

The `VerifyRequestEnvelope` should successfully deserialize V1-formatted requests, or there should be clear documentation of the expected V1 body format.

## Environment

- x402 SDK: `@x402/core`, `@x402/evm` (official Coinbase SDK)
- Client: Node.js with `viem` for EIP-712 signing
- Chain: Avalanche Fuji (43113)
- USDC: `0x5425890298aed601595a70AB815c96711a31Bc65`

## Workaround

We use the `payment-signature` header (V2 protocol) which works correctly. Filed a PR on the SnowRail middleware to adopt this approach: https://github.com/Colombia-Blockchain/snowrail-core/pull/91

title: fix: serialize authorization.value as decimal string instead of hex
body:
From Spec
https://github.com/coinbase/x402/blob/main/specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md#1-assettransfermethod-eip-3009

The value field must be in decimal format.
```
  "payload": {
    "signature": "0x2d6a7588d6acca505cbf0d9a4a227e0c52c6c34008c8e8986a1283259764173608a2ce6496642e377d6da8dbbf5836e9bd15092f9ecab05ded3d6293af148b571c",
    "authorization": {
      "from": "0x857b06519E91e3A54538791bDbb0E22373e36b66",
      "to": "0x209693Bc6afc0C5328bA36FaF03C514EF312287C",
      "value": "10000",
      "validAfter": "1740672089",
      "validBefore": "1740672154",
      "nonce": "0xf3746613c2d920b5fdabc0856f2aeb2d4f88ee6037b8cc5d04a71a4462f13480"
    }
  }
```

The `authorization.value` field was being serialized as a hex string (e.g., `"0x1234"`) due to `alloy_primitives::U256`'s default serde behavior. However, the x402 protocol expects this field to be a decimal string (e.g., `"1000000"`) for cross-language interoperability with other SDKs (e.g., TypeScript).

# Overview

This PR refactors the x402-rs project from a single monolithic crate into a modular workspace architecture. This change improves maintainability, allows selective dependency usage, and provides better separation of concerns.

# Changes

## New Workspace Structure

The project is now organized as a Cargo workspace with the following crates:

**Core Crates:**
- `x402-types` - Core protocol types, facilitator traits, and utilities (foundation for all implementations)
- `x402-axum` - Axum middleware for protecting routes with x402 payments
- `x402-reqwest` - Reqwest middleware for transparent x402 payment handling
- `x402-facilitator-local` - Facilitator implementation

**Blockchain Support:**
- `x402-chain-eip155` - EVM/EIP-155 chain support (Ethereum, Base, Polygon, etc.)
- `x402-chain-solana` - Solana blockchain support
- `x402-chain-aptos` - Aptos blockchain support

**Deployment:**
- `facilitator` - Production-ready facilitator server binary (not published to crates.io due to git-only dependencies)

### Key Improvements

1. **Modular Dependencies**: Users can now depend only on the crates they need (e.g., just `x402-types` + `x402-chain-eip155` for EVM-only support)

2. **Better Organization**: Chain-specific code is isolated in dedicated crates with clear feature flags (`client`, `server`, `facilitator`)

3. **Workspace Configuration**: Shared dependencies and version management through workspace-level configuration

4. **Updated Documentation**

5. **CI/CD Improvements**: Multi-architecture Docker builds (AMD64 + ARM64)

### Migration Guide

**Before:**
```toml
[dependencies]
x402-rs = { version = "0.12" }
```

**After:**
```toml
[dependencies]
x402-types = "1.0"
x402-chain-eip155 = { version = "1.0", features = ["client"] }
x402-chain-solana = { version = "1.0", features = ["client"] }
```

### Breaking Changes

- The main `x402-rs` crate is no longer relevant to use
- Import paths have changed (e.g., `x402_rs::networks` → `x402_types::networks`)
- Feature flags are now per-crate rather than global

### Testing

All existing functionality has been preserved. The refactoring maintains backward compatibility at the protocol level while providing a more flexible architecture for future development.

body:
## Add Aptos Support to Facilitator                                                                            
                                                                                                                 
  This PR adds complete Aptos blockchain support to the x402-rs facilitator, enabling x402 payment verification  
  and settlement on Aptos mainnet and testnet.                                                                   
                                                                                                                 
  ### Changes                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                 
  #### Core Aptos Integration                                                                                    
  - **New chain provider** (`src/chain/aptos.rs`): Implements `ChainProviderOps` for Aptos with Ed25519 key      
  handling, REST client integration, and fee payer (sponsor) support for gasless transactions                    
  - **CAIP-2 compliance**: Uses standard chain identifiers (`aptos:1` for mainnet, `aptos:2` for testnet)        
  - **Configuration support** (`src/config.rs`): Added `ChainConfig::Aptos` variant with RPC URL and private key 
  configuration                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                 
  #### V2 Exact Payment Scheme                                                                                   
  - **New scheme implementation** (`src/scheme/v2_aptos_exact/`): Implements the "exact" payment scheme for Aptos
   fungible assets                                                                                               
  - **Fungible asset transfers**: Uses `0x1::primary_fungible_store::transfer` for token movements               
  - **Sponsored transactions**: Facilitator pays gas fees, enabling gasless payments for users                   
  - **Transaction verification**: Validates BCS-encoded transactions before settlement                           
                                                                                                                 
  #### Dependencies                                                                                              
  - **Aptos dependencies** (`Cargo.toml`): Added `aptos-types`, `aptos-crypto`, `aptos-rest-client`, and         
  `move-core-types` using git tag `aptos-node-v1.39.2` (stable release)                                          
  - **Tokio compatibility patch** (`patches/aptos-runtimes/`): Local patch to resolve incompatibility between    
  aptos-core's tokio 1.35 and our tokio 1.45 by removing deprecated `disable_lifo_slot()` call                   
                                                                                                                 
  #### Developer Experience                                                                                      
  - **Network helpers** (`src/networks.rs`): Added `KnownNetworkAptos` trait with `.aptos()` and                 
  `.aptos_testnet()` convenience methods                                                                         
  - **Consistent API**: Follows existing patterns established for EVM and Solana chains                          
                                                                                                                 
  ### Setup Instructions                                                                                         
                                                                                                                 
  #### 1. Generate an Aptos Private Key                                                                          
                                                                                                                 
  Using Aptos CLI:                                                                                               
  ```bash                                                                                                        
  aptos key generate --output-file aptos-key.json                                                                
                                                                                                                 
  Or using the TypeScript SDK:                                                                                   
  import { Account } from "@aptos-labs/ts-sdk";                                                                  
  const account = Account.generate();                                                                            
  console.log(`Private key: 0x${account.privateKey.toString()}`);                                                
  console.log(`Address: ${account.accountAddress.toString()}`);    
```                                              
                                                                                                                 
  2. Fund the Fee Payer Account                                                                                  
                                                                                                                 
  The fee payer account sponsors gas for user transactions, so it needs APT balance:                             
                                                                                                                 
  Testnet (aptos:2):                                                                                             
  - Visit https://aptos.dev/en/network/faucet                                                                    
  - Enter your account address                                                                                   
  - Request testnet APT                                                                                          
                                                                                                                 
  Mainnet (aptos:1):                                                                                             
  - Purchase APT from an exchange                                                                                
  - Transfer to your fee payer account address                                                                   
  - Recommended: Start with at least 1 APT for gas (~100,000 transactions at current gas prices)                 
                                                                                                                 
  3. Configure the Facilitator                                                                                   
                                                                                                                 
  Add to your config.json:                                                                                       
 ```                                                                                                                
  {                                                                                                              
    "chains": {                                                                                                  
      "aptos:2": {                                                                                               
        "rpc": "https://fullnode.testnet.aptoslabs.com/v1",                                                      
        "fee_payer": "$APTOS_FEE_PAYER_KEY"                                                                      
      },                                                                                                         
      "aptos:1": {                                                                                               
        "rpc": "https://fullnode.mainnet.aptoslabs.com/v1",                                                      
        "fee_payer": "$APTOS_MAINNET_FEE_PAYER_KEY"                                                              
      }                                                                                                          
    },                                                                                                           
    "schemes": [                                                                                                 
      {                                                                                                          
        "id": "v2-aptos-exact",                                                                                  
        "chains": "aptos:*"                                                                                      
      }                                                                                                          
    ]                                                                                                            
  }                                                                                                              
  ```                                                                                                               
  Set environment variables:                                                                                     
  export APTOS_FEE_PAYER_KEY=0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY_HERE                                                             
  export APTOS_MAINNET_FEE_PAYER_KEY=0xYOUR_MAINNET_KEY_HERE                                                     
                                                                                                                 
  Security Note: Never commit private keys to version control. Always use environment variables or secure key    
  management systems.                                                                                            
                                                                                                                 
  4. Monitor Gas Usage                                                                                           
                                                                                                                 
  The fee payer account pays gas for all settled transactions. Monitor the balance:                              
```bash                                                                                                            
  # Using Aptos CLI     
                                                                                
  aptos account list --account YOUR_FEE_PAYER_ADDRESS                                                            
                                                                                                                 
  # Or check via REST API                                                                                        
  curl https://fullnode.testnet.aptoslabs.com/v1/accounts/YOUR_ADDRESS/resources                                 
```                                                                                                            
  Set up alerts when balance drops below a threshold to ensure uninterrupted service.                            
                                                                                                                 
  Usage Example                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                 
  Client code:           
```bash                                                                                        
  use x402_rs::networks::{KnownNetworkAptos, USDC};                                                              
  use x402_rs::scheme::v2_aptos_exact::V2AptosExact;                                                             
  use x402_rs::chain::ChainId;                                                                                   
                                                                                                                 
  // USDC on Aptos testnet                                                                                       
  let usdc = USDC::aptos_testnet();                                                                              
  let price = V2AptosExact::price_tag(                                                                           
      "0x1234...",  // pay_to address (merchant)                                                                 
      usdc.amount(1_000_000),  // 1 USDC (6 decimals)                                                            
  );            
```                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                 
  Testing                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                 
  - ✅ Cargo build succeeds with new dependencies                                                                
  - ✅ All Aptos dependencies resolve correctly using git tag                                                    
  - ✅ Tokio compatibility patch applies cleanly                                                                 
  - ✅ Successfully tested with Aptos testnet                                                                    
                                                                                                                 
  Notes                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                 
  Sponsored Transactions                                                                                         
                                                                                                                 
  Unlike EVM and Solana implementations where users pay their own gas fees, Aptos transactions in this           
  implementation are sponsored by the facilitator's fee payer account. This enables:                             
  - Gasless payments: Users don't need APT in their wallets                                                      
  - Better UX: Users only need the payment token (e.g., USDC)                                                    
  - Operational cost: Facilitator operators must maintain APT balance for gas
  - An alternative implementation for sponsorship would be to integrate with Geomi gas station - this would allow for facilitators to not need to fund and manage the fee payer.  See https://geomi.dev/docs/gas-stations                                
                                                                                                                 
  Git Dependencies                                                                                               
                                                                                                                 
  Aptos core libraries are not published to crates.io (only placeholder 0.0.0 versions exist). This PR uses git  
  tags instead of commit hashes for better readability and maintainability.                                      
                                                                                                                 
  Tokio Compatibility Patch                                                                                      
                                                                                                                 
  The patch in patches/aptos-runtimes/ is necessary because:                                                     
  - aptos-core uses tokio 1.35 which has the disable_lifo_slot() method                                          
  - This project uses tokio 1.45 where that method was removed                                                   
  - The patch is minimal (removes one line) and well-documented                                                  
  - This can be removed when aptos-core upgrades to tokio 1.45+

body:
# Fix: Register schemes for all chains matching a wildcard pattern

## Description
This PR fixes a bug where `SchemeRegistry` would only register a scheme handler for the *first* chain that matched a wildcard pattern (e.g., `eip155:*`), ignoring all subsequent matching chains. This caused `Unsupported scheme` errors for any chain other than the first one found in the configuration.

## Root Cause
- `ChainRegistry::by_chain_id_pattern` was using `find_map`, which returns `Option` (the first match).
- `SchemeRegistry::build` was expecting a single `ChainProvider` from that call.

## Changes
- **`src/chain/mod.rs`**: Updated `by_chain_id_pattern` to return `Vec<ChainProvider>` instead of `Option<ChainProvider>`. It now filters and collects *all* matching chains.
- **`src/scheme/mod.rs`**: Updated `SchemeRegistry::build` to iterate over the returned vector of chain providers and register a handler for each one.

## Issue
Fixes `Unsupported scheme` error when multiple chains are configured under a wildcard scheme (e.g., Polygon Mainnet and Amoy).

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update

## How Has This Been Tested?
1. Configured `config.json` with multiple EVM chains (e.g., `eip155:137` and `eip155:80002`).
2. Configured schemes with a wildcard pattern `"chains": "eip155:*"`.
3. Verified that the `/verify` endpoint now correctly processes requests for *both* chains, whereas previously it would fail for the second one.

This PR refactors the network registry from `src/chain/chain_id.rs` into a dedicated `src/networks.rs` module, introducing a trait-based architecture for better code organization and extensibility.

### New Module: `src/networks.rs`
